notation_and_syntax.notes: Minimization and maximization use the same alpha>=1 convention with reciprocal inequalities.

evidence: Enumerated all 33,868 simple undirected graphs through six vertices; every constructed matching was disjoint and maximal, every endpoint set was a cover, and every result satisfied size at most twice exhaustive optimum.

empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Finite graph enumeration validates this implementation domain but does not replace the universal mathematical proof or establish production performance.

pedagogical_review.notes: The Level-II chapter builds from formal optimization definitions to a complete two-approximation proof and production evidence contract, includes ten distinct ratio, boundary, certificate, scheme, probability, bicriteria, and timeout examples, and ends with five progressive exercises and complete answers.

limitations: Internal source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical review only; no external academic, complexity-theory, optimization, numerical-analysis, security, performance, or operational review is claimed. Results remain conditional on the declared instance class, feasibility, objective direction and domain, arithmetic, bound, randomization, transformation, runtime, and production-path assumptions.
